description: One entry on the dock. It does **two** things when clicked -- it opens a page and it swaps the shell -- and each exists without the other, which is why they are two columns: `sidebar` is the shell, `link_type`/`link_to`/`url` is the page. The ordinary row fills one; filling both is the override, for a page whose own module is not the shell you want. Every row also carries its own `icon` and `title`, so the rail reads the way its author wrote it -- blank at an upper layer means inherit. What a row points at *is* its identity, and none of it is stored: re-labelling cannot detach a row from itself, and re-pointing is not an edit but a different row. The same rows at all three layers -- the app's own dock, the site's arrangement and one person's -- told apart by the parent `Dock`, never by the row.

fields.description: The shell this entry selects -- the panel that comes up beside it. Blank derives the shell from the module that owns what the row opens, which is the ordinary case for a workspace row and the whole of how a companion's pin lands a person in the companion's shell. A `Link` whose target need not exist as a document: most modules have a computed base and no `Sidebar` row at all, so this names a shell rather than referencing one, which is why link validation on a `Dock` is a deliberate no-op.
fields.label: Sidebar

fields.description: What kind of page this entry opens, if it opens one. Spelled the way `Sidebar Item` spells it, so `frappe.ui.sidebar_item.get_route(row)` takes a dock row unchanged. `Sidebar` is deliberately absent as a value: a module entry is a row with `sidebar` filled and no target, and naming the module in a type value as well would be redundant.
fields.label: Link Type

fields.description: The record this entry opens, in the doctype `link_type` names.
fields.label: Link To

fields.description: Where a web address entry goes. A URL row has no shell and is gated by nothing.
fields.label: URL

fields.description: What the rail draws this entry with. Required when the row *adds* an entry, because nothing below it holds one; optional when it references an entry a lower layer already has, where blank means inherit and filled is an override.
fields.label: Icon

fields.description: How this entry reads on the rail. Required when the row adds and optional when it references, exactly as `icon` is -- and outside the row's identity, so re-labelling can never detach a row from itself.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: This row *is* the entry, rather than an opinion about one a lower layer holds. Stored rather than inferred from the row carrying a body: under partial opinions a reference may carry an icon and no title, so body-presence stops telling the two apart -- and a reference to a row the app has since deleted would resurrect as a label-less button.
fields.label: Added

fields.description: Kept in the row so an explicitly hidden entry stays hidden when its app later adds entries, instead of reappearing because it is simply absent.
fields.label: Hidden

name: Dock Item
